description: Captures rows and ongoing row-level changes from Microsoft SQL Server tables using SQL Server's built-in Change Tracking feature.

spec.sslPolicy: DSN always sets encrypt=true and TrustServerCertificate=true; the connector logs the negotiated encrypt_option from sys.dm_exec_connections but never fails on it
spec.tunnelSupport: Optional SSH forwarding (networkTunnel.sshForwarding) via flow-network-tunnel; a custom HostDialer redirects TCP dials to the local tunnel listener while keeping the real hostname in TLS SNI and the TDS LOGIN7 ServerName

defaultSchedule.description: advanced.polling_interval — Go duration string, minimum 100ms, must not exceed sqlcapture.StreamingFenceInterval. Polls run continuously inside each StreamToFence cycle.

artifacts: Database-level Change Tracking: ALTER DATABASE <db> SET CHANGE_TRACKING = ON (CHANGE_RETENTION = 2 DAYS, AUTO_CLEANUP = ON) — issued by the connector when CT is not already enabled
Per-table Change Tracking: ALTER TABLE <schema>.<table> ENABLE CHANGE_TRACKING — issued by the connector for each bound table that does not already have it
SQL Server's internal change-tracking side tables backing sys.change_tracking_tables / CHANGETABLE() for each enabled table
continuity.customerSideAccrual: The internal CT side table for each enabled table accumulates one row per changed row. Growth is bounded by the database's CHANGE_RETENTION setting and SQL Server's own AUTO_CLEANUP task, which prunes on a time basis regardless of whether we are consuming — so unlike a Postgres replication slot or an unread binlog, nothing grows without bound because we stopped reading. Enabling CT does add synchronous per-DML write overhead to the customer's transactions for as long as it stays enabled.
continuity.ourSideLoss: Our resume position is a per-table SYS_CHANGE_VERSION integer. On every poll the connector reads sys.change_tracking_tables.min_valid_version for each table; if our stored version is below it, the changes in between have been auto-cleaned and are unrecoverable. The connector does not error out: it logs 'change tracking data expired for table', emits a sqlcapture.TableDropEvent with that cause, deactivates the table and drops its entry from the cursor — which forces a fresh backfill of that table. The same path fires if CT is turned off for a table (the table disappears from sys.change_tracking_tables). Data changed during the gap is therefore lost as change events and only recovered as of the re-backfill's current state.
continuity.resumeWindow: The database's CHANGE_RETENTION setting — 2 days when the connector enables Change Tracking itself; whatever value the DBA chose when CT was already on. Idle tables are protected beyond that: the connector fast-forwards their cursors to the current version on every poll (via a batched EXISTS probe) specifically so idle tables don't fall behind min_valid_version.
continuity.notes: The connector enables Change Tracking itself when the configured user has permission (both at the database level and per table), and only errors ('Change Tracking is not enabled ... and user X cannot enable it') when it cannot — so the DBA is a fallback, not a precondition. Nothing is torn down on shutdown: Close() on the replication stream and on the DB handle only closes the connection; CT stays enabled on the database and all tables, and there is no ALTER ... DISABLE CHANGE_TRACKING anywhere in the connector. Acknowledge() is a no-op — there is no consumption-driven server-side trim to fall behind on. Prerequisites additionally refuse to run against a read-only/secondary database because CT metadata is incoherent there.

discovery.method: SQL Server system catalog + INFORMATION_SCHEMA queries, re-run periodically while the capture is live (rediscovery_interval, default 15m, jittered)
discovery.querySketch: Table list: by default SELECT DISTINCT schema/table by joining sys.change_tracking_tables -> sys.tables -> sys.schemas -> INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES, so only CT-ENABLED tables are listed; with discover_tables_without_ct set it degrades to a plain INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES scan. Per-table details are then fetched in chunks of 100 tables against INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES / .COLUMNS / .KEY_COLUMN_USAGE+.TABLE_CONSTRAINTS / sys.columns(is_computed=1), the chunk predicate being a disjunction of (schema=@p AND table=@p) equalities with a padded trailing chunk so one cached plan serves every chunk.
excludes: tables not matching discoveryFilters.table_patterns when that list is non-empty
tables with no primary key — retained in the discovery map but marked OmitBinding, because Change Tracking requires a primary key
discovery.allowlist: discoveryFilters.include_schemas is intersected in-query; the default CT-only table list is itself an implicit allowlist

streams.name: <schema>.<table> (CT-enabled, primary-keyed)
primaryKey: <table primary key columns, in ordinal order>

schedules.role: change polling inside each streaming fence

schedule.description: advanced.polling_interval; each StreamToFence cycle loops polling until the fence deadline, then does one final catch-up poll to the fence version
advanced.rediscovery_interval, jittered so simultaneously-started captures don't hit the catalog in lockstep

backfill.querySketch: Keyed chunked scan of the BASE TABLE (not CHANGETABLE), built by the shared sqlserver backfill helper: SELECT all columns FROM <schema>.<table> ordered by the primary key, with a resume predicate comparing the key tuple against the last emitted row key. Datetime-typed key columns are bound as typed datetime parameters (not formatted strings) so the resume predicate can index-seek. Rows are emitted with _meta.op = 'c' and source.snapshot = true, and carry no CT version.
backfill.chunking: advanced.backfill_chunk_size rows per query (default 50000); the chunk is the last chunk when it returns fewer rows than that. A 2-hour watchdog, reset on every row, cancels a query that stops making progress. A keyless-backfill mode exists in the shared code and synthesizes 'B%019d' offset row keys, but CT bindings always have a primary key.

incremental.resumeTokenKind: Per-table int64 SYS_CHANGE_VERSION, checkpointed as a JSON object keyed by 'schema.table' (a removed binding is written back as null to delete its entry). Validated each poll against sys.change_tracking_tables.min_valid_version.

incremental.resumeTokenKind: Per-table int64 SYS_CHANGE_VERSION starting at CHANGE_TRACKING_CURRENT_VERSION() as of table activation, so only changes made after the capture was configured are ever seen.

authTierRationale: The only credential is a SQL Server host/port, username, password and database name — a single self-serve connection string with no OAuth app registration and no refresh token, so T1_SIMPLE. The real setup cost is privilege, not credential complexity: the user needs VIEW CHANGE TRACKING and SELECT on the captured tables, and enough privilege for ALTER DATABASE ... SET CHANGE_TRACKING = ON and ALTER TABLE ... ENABLE CHANGE_TRACKING if Change Tracking is not already on, otherwise a DBA must run those first. That is a permissions prerequisite, not a higher auth tier.

unionMisfits.description: The poll/log dichotomy does not fit. This connector polls (every 500ms by default, via repeated CHANGETABLE queries) but consumes a durable, retention-bounded, server-side change record with a monotonic resume cursor and real expiry semantics — which is why continuity matters at all. Recorded as 'log' because the continuity questions the schema cares about (retention expiry, resume window, server-side artifacts) all apply, but the transport mechanic is polling.

The `changes` PullSpec has no way to express that the change feed is KEY-ONLY and must be re-joined to the live base table to get values. That is the single most consequential fact about Change Tracking versus CDC and it is currently only representable in prose. It implies (a) update/insert values are the row's state AT QUERY TIME, not at the change version — several rapid updates collapse to one read of the current row, and (b) a row deleted between the change and the poll yields NULLs from the outer join.

proposedShape.changeQuerySketch: SELECT CT.SYS_CHANGE_VERSION, CT.SYS_CHANGE_OPERATION, CT.<pk cols>, T.<other cols> FROM CHANGETABLE(CHANGES <table>, @from) AS CT LEFT OUTER JOIN <table> AS T ON CT.<pk> = T.<pk> WHERE CT.SYS_CHANGE_VERSION > @from AND <= @to ORDER BY CT.SYS_CHANGE_VERSION

unionMisfits.description: The cursor is not per-stream; it is one shared JSON map of stream ID -> version checkpointed by the connector as a whole, and entries are added on table activation and written back as null on removal. The schema models resume state as a per-stream scalar.

The disposition is endpoint-configurable, not fixed per stream: the top-level `historyMode` flag switches the whole capture from reduced final-state documents (merge, with deletes reducing to a delete) to unreduced change events (append).

Artifacts here are not objects the connector created and owns, they are a MODE toggled on customer objects (a database option and a per-table option). 'releasedOnShutdown: false' is accurate but understates it — there is no release path at all, and disabling CT is a customer action with its own consequences for any other CT consumer.

There is a third outcome besides 'sync' and 'fail' that the schema cannot express: on retention expiry or CT being disabled, the connector emits a TableDropEvent, silently deactivates just that binding and continues capturing the rest. The affected collection stops receiving data (pending re-backfill) while the capture reports healthy.

abstained.streams[].name: The stream list is entirely a function of the customer's own catalog — discovery lists CT-enabled tables from sys.change_tracking_tables. No stream name is hardcoded anywhere in the connector, so both entries are archetypes, not real streams.
abstained.streams[0].pull.backfill.querySketch (ex: The backfill SQL is built by the shared helper go/capture/sqlserver/backfill.BuildBackfillQuery, which was not part of the mined directory. Chunk size, key ordering, the datetime-parameter binding fix and the resume-key semantics are all evidenced from this connector and its CHANGELOG, but the literal query text and the exact resume predicate are not.
abstained.execution.continuity.customerSideAccrual: SQL Server's CT auto-cleanup is a background task the connector neither drives nor observes beyond reading min_valid_version, so the actual on-disk growth rate of the internal side tables (and the synchronous per-DML write cost of enabling CT) cannot be quantified from this source.
abstained.transports[0].spec.sslPolicy (enforcemen: TrustServerCertificate=true is hardcoded, so the TLS certificate is never verified; whether the platform layers any additional verification on top is outside this directory. prerequisiteConnectionEncryption only logs the negotiated encrypt_option and always returns nil.
abstained.streams[].pull.backfill handoff ordering: ActivateTable records CHANGE_TRACKING_CURRENT_VERSION() for a newly-added table and backfill scans the base table thereafter, so the handoff is 'note the version, then scan, then replay changes above that version'. The precise interleaving of backfill chunks with StreamToFence cycles is orchestrated by the shared sqlcapture driver, which was not mined.
abstained.streams[].primaryKeyKind for keyless tab: Keyless tables are marked OmitBinding during discovery and the connector's FallbackCollectionKey() returns an empty slice with the comment that CT requires primary keys, so no keyless stream archetype is emitted. A TestBackfillWithoutKey and a TestKeylessDiscovery snapshot exist but their contents were not read.
